Alert complexity of each person-year

Source: R/plcvol.R
alrtcx.Rd

Counts the distinct alert configurations among a person-year's records. Each record carries flags (in Ontario's records the mental health, suicide risk and suicide watch alerts); its configuration is the tuple of the flags, (1, 0, 0) for a mental health alert alone, coded as the text "100". Alert complexity is the number of distinct configurations the person-year's records span, and cx, complexity of two or more, is the treatment of Ruhela (2026, Appendix H).

Usage

alrtcx(flags, id, keep = NULL)

Arguments

flags

The alert flags of each record: a data frame, list or matrix with one column per flag; each value 1 / 0, TRUE / FALSE or yes / no text (case and surrounding space ignored).

id

The person-year of each record, as for plcvol().

keep

NULL to count every configuration, or the configurations to count, as codes such as "100" (one digit per flag).

Value

A data frame of class alrtcx, one row per person-year in order of first appearance: id, n (records), ac (distinct configurations among those counted), cx (1 when ac >= 2), and anyal (1 when any record carries an alert).

Details

cx = 1 holds exactly when two records are in different configurations: a record without alerts and one with a single alert give cx = 1, while one record with all three alerts gives cx = 0. The count measures change of alert state over the records, not alerts held at once (proof("alrtcx")). It does not depend on the order of the records or on an injective relabelling of the configurations, never falls when a record is added, and is at most the number of configurations allowed. keep restricts the count to the configurations given (the published analysis counts the six seen in the release and ignores any other). The work is O(n log n).

References

Ruhela, V. S. (2026). Alert complexity and placement volatility in Ontario restrictive confinement data. Major research paper, Centre for Criminology and Sociolegal Studies, University of Toronto.

Examples

f <- data.frame(mh = c("Yes", "No", "No", "Yes"),
                sr = c("No", "No", "Yes", "Yes"),
                sw = c("No", "No", "No", "Yes"))
alrtcx(f, id = c(1, 1, 2, 3))
#> alrtcx: 3 person-years; 1 (33.3%) span two or more alert configurations
#>  id n ac cx anyal
#>   1 2  2  1     1
#>   2 1  1  0     1
#>   3 1  1  0     1
